title: I recommended Finch to my psychiatrist!
body: Finch is the perfect reminder for me for doing simple everyday things. Being diagnosed with dysthymia (persistent depression) and AD(H)D I constantly need external taps on the shoulders to remind me of getting me through the day. I am in my own head constantly and am in constant need to know what’s coming because I might forget things. Alarms don’t work, because I forget alarms, so I’d need an alarm to even set an alarm. Finch takes care of this! It also has a great reward system if you are susceptive to goals and unlocks in videogames for instance. It works because you actually start to care for your pet. Mine’s called Pickle and I immediately bonded with him because he’s “mine”. I don’t forget my goals for the day either because I want him to do well, and I want to give him the same kindness I would like for myself. So in that way, he is also a portrayal of myself. Nothing has ever worked before in such a way that I would actually take care of myself in this way. You could easily check all the goals you have for the day even if you don’t do them, but somehow I can’t simply lie to Pickle, so I actually go do the simple tasks I’ve set for the day. I recently started adding more important goals to a few days of the week, like decluttering my desk, showering on set days of the week, and spending 5 minutes tidying my home on all days. And it works for me. It really made me more calm and confident in being able to set small goals for myself and actually do them. I already know how to take care of myself, I just needed reminders, and it does just that. I can’t thank the developers enough because it really really helped me grow with my healing journey. It also comes with a Finch Plus+ subscription, but if you don’t want that it’s not intrusive at all, you can just get less things on a daily basis. The items are still available for everyone, just less of them and they aren’t locked behind a paywall. I even recommended Finch to my psychiatrist. She looked into it and she’s gonna recommend it to a few other patients. I can confidently say it makes my days better. If you are struggling with structure and selfcare, do yourself a favor and give it a try.

title: This app was the pivot point to a healthy wellbeing
body:
Finch changed my life, it completely transformed my entire view on selfcare, and what that means. In my journey (now 65 continuous days) I started out with small tasks that made me feel a lot better of myself. Today these tasks have become a part of my regular schedule, without even thinking about them. My goals are getting more and more ambitious, and it just feels too good completing something. 

When i started i was not feeling good. I was smoking weed everyday to substitute my deleted social media apps which i was trying to quit. Now, i’ve changed my relation ship with weed, only allowing myself to smoke when im satisfied with my day (and only when i feel good) I am reading my book every night, meeting friends regularly, waking up early and going to bed early, just to name a few. (there’s much more but i don’t want to write too long of a review) 

The user experience is amazing, not distracting or asking you for much attention, just there to serve you in your selfcare journey. And of course it’s very cute. I’ve gotten rid of some streaming services in order to buy myself finch plus, which is nice to have. (because why wouldn’t spent some money each month on an app that makes me feel really good? 

Thank you finch!!

title: This app deserves more than 5 stars
body: It’s not only the app, but the whole community that makes Finch so awesome. The app itself helps me every day to get things done, check in with my feelings, use writing as a healthy coping mechanism and handle my anxiety the right way. In addition, the Facebook group and discord server make me feel like im part of a big wholesome family where everyone supports each other
